syntax: ORDER BY name COLLATE NOCASE, id
summary: Compare ASCII text without case distinctions while retaining its original spelling.
documentation: A COLLATE clause selects the comparison rule for an expression. SQLite’s built-in NOCASE folds ASCII A through Z during comparison, so mixed-case ASCII names can sort together without rewriting the selected text.
inputs: labels(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL).
returns: id and the original name, ordered with NOCASE comparison and id as tie-breaker.
caution: Built-in NOCASE is not full Unicode case folding or locale-aware sorting. Accented uppercase and lowercase letters can still compare differently. A collation changes comparison, not stored or displayed spelling.
scenarios: Sort an ASCII-oriented internal code list with mixed case.
Keep original customer-entered label spelling in an export.
Apply a documented comparison rule to a local report without updating rows.
title: Sort labels without changing spelling
problem: Select id and name. Sort name ascending using COLLATE NOCASE, then id ascending when names compare equal. Preserve the original text. Follow SQLite’s ASCII-only case folding.
hint: Put COLLATE NOCASE on the name expression in ORDER BY.
goal: Use COLLATE NOCASE or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
